question_text: Which of the following is a fundamental concept of object-oriented programming?
explanation: Encapsulation is a core OOP concept that combines data and methods into a single unit.

question_text: Which OOP concept allows an object to hide its internal implementation details?
explanation: Abstraction hides implementation details and exposes essential features.

question_text: Which feature allows a class to acquire properties and methods from another class?
explanation: Inheritance allows a subclass to acquire members from its superclass.

question_text: Which OOP concept allows one interface or method name to represent different behaviors?
explanation: Polymorphism means one interface can represent multiple forms of behavior.

question_text: What is the main purpose of encapsulation?
option_b: To combine data and methods and control access
explanation: Encapsulation bundles data and related methods and controls access to the data.

question_text: Which programming approach primarily focuses on functions and procedures?
explanation: Procedure-oriented programming organizes programs mainly around functions and procedures.

question_text: Which approach provides data hiding as an important programming feature?
option_c: Both always provide identical data hiding
explanation: OOP supports data hiding through access control and encapsulation.

question_text: Java is commonly described as which type of programming language?
explanation: Java bytecode can run on any platform that has a compatible JVM.

question_text: Which Java feature allows the same bytecode to run on different operating systems?
explanation: Platform independence is achieved through the JVM executing Java bytecode.

question_text: Which feature of Java automatically manages unused memory?
explanation: Java garbage collection automatically reclaims memory occupied by unreachable objects.

question_text: What is the full form of JVM?
explanation: JVM stands for Java Virtual Machine.

question_text: Which component converts Java source code into bytecode?
explanation: The Java compiler javac converts source code into bytecode.

question_text: Which component is responsible for executing Java bytecode?
explanation: The JVM loads and executes Java bytecode.

question_text: Which package contains the tools required to develop Java applications?
explanation: JDK includes development tools such as the Java compiler along with runtime components.

question_text: What is the relationship between JRE and JVM?
explanation: JRE includes the JVM and libraries required to run Java applications.

question_text: Which method is the usual entry point of a standalone Java application?
explanation: The main method is the standard entry point of a standalone Java application.

question_text: Which of the following is an integer literal in Java?
explanation: 12 without a decimal point is an integer literal.

question_text: Which of the following is not a primitive data type in Java?
explanation: String is a class and not a primitive data type.

question_text: Which variable is declared inside a method and is accessible only within that method block?
explanation: A local variable is declared inside a method or block and has local scope.

question_text: What is the result of the expression 10 % 3 in Java?
explanation: The modulus operator returns the remainder after division; 10 divided by 3 leaves remainder 1.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int x = 5; System.out.println(x++ + ++x); } }
explanation: x++ returns 5 and increments x to 6. ++x increments it to 7 and returns 7. Therefore 5 + 7 = 12.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int a = 10; if(a > 5) { if(a < 15) System.out.print("A"); else System.out.print("B"); } } }
explanation: Both conditions are true, so A is printed. The else belongs to the inner if.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int n = 2; switch(n) { case 1: System.out.print("A"); case 2: System.out.print("B"); case 3: System.out.print("C"); } } }
explanation: Execution starts at case 2 and falls through to case 3 because there are no break statements.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int i = 1; while(i <= 3) { System.out.print(i); i++; } } }
explanation: The loop prints 1, 2 and 3. It stops when i becomes 4.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int i = 5; do { System.out.print(i); } while(i < 5); } }
explanation: A do-while loop executes its body at least once before checking the condition.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { for(int i = 0; i < 5; i++) { if(i == 3) break; System.out.print(i); } } }
explanation: The loop prints 0, 1 and 2. When i becomes 3, break terminates the loop.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { for(int i = 0; i < 5; i++) { if(i == 2) continue; System.out.print(i); } } }
explanation: When i equals 2, continue skips the remaining statements in that iteration.

question_text: What happens when this code is compiled? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int x = 5; if(x = 5) System.out.print("Yes"); } }
explanation: The assignment expression x = 5 has an int value. Java requires a boolean condition in an if statement.

question_text: What happens when this switch statement is compiled? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int x = 2; switch(x) { case 1: break; case 2: break; case 2: break; } } }
explanation: A traditional switch statement cannot contain duplicate case labels with the same constant value.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { if(false); System.out.print("Hello"); } }
explanation: The semicolon immediately after if represents an empty statement. The print statement executes independently.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int x = 1; while(x < 4) { System.out.print(x); x++; } } }
explanation: The loop prints 1, 2 and 3 before the condition becomes false.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { for(int i = 1; i <= 3; i++) { System.out.print(i * i); } } }
explanation: The squares of 1, 2 and 3 are 1, 4 and 9. They are printed consecutively as 149.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { for(int i = 1; i <= 2; i++) { for(int j = 1; j <= 2; j++) { System.out.print(i + j); } } } }
explanation: The sums are 2, 3, 3 and 4 in that order. Therefore the output is 2334.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int x = 0; if(x == 0) System.out.print("Zero"); else System.out.print("Nonzero"); } }
explanation: The condition x == 0 is true, so Zero is printed.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int day = 2; switch(day) { case 1: System.out.print("Monday"); break; case 2: System.out.print("Tuesday"); break; default: System.out.print("Invalid"); } } }
explanation: The value of day is 2, so case 2 executes and prints Tuesday.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int x = 3; System.out.println(x++ * 2); } }
explanation: Post-increment uses the original value 3 in the expression. Therefore 3 multiplied by 2 equals 6.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int x = 4; System.out.println(++x + x++); } }
explanation: ++x increments x to 5 and returns 5. x++ returns 5 and then increments x. The sum is 10.

question_text: What is the main problem in this code? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int i = 1; while(i <= 3) { System.out.println(i); } } }
option_b: The loop executes exactly three times
explanation: The value of i is never updated, so i remains 1 and the condition stays true indefinitely.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int i = 1; do { System.out.print(i); i++; } while(i < 1); } }
explanation: The do block executes once and prints 1. Then i becomes 2 and the condition is false.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int a = 17; int b = 5; System.out.println(a / b + a % b); } }
explanation: Integer division gives 17 / 5 = 3 and remainder gives 17 % 5 = 2. Their sum is 5.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int x = 10; double y = x; System.out.println(y); } }
explanation: Widening conversion automatically converts int to double, producing 10.0.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { double x = 9.8; int y = (int)x; System.out.println(y); } }
explanation: Explicit casting from double to int removes the fractional part; it does not round the value.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int x = 5; x += 3; System.out.println(x); } }
explanation: The compound assignment x += 3 is equivalent to x = x + 3.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println(10 + 20 + "Java"); } }
explanation: Addition is evaluated from left to right. First 10 + 20 gives 30, then string concatenation produces 30Java.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println("Java" + 10 + 20); } }
explanation: String concatenation starts with Java. Both 10 and 20 are then appended as strings.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int a = 5; System.out.println(a > 3 && a < 10); } }
explanation: Both relational conditions are true, so the logical AND operator returns true.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int x = 5; System.out.println(x > 10 || x < 10); } }
explanation: The first condition is false and the second is true. False OR true gives true.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int x = 5; System.out.println(!(x > 3)); } }
explanation: Since x > 3 is true, the logical NOT operator changes it to false.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println(5 & 3); } }
explanation: Binary 5 is 101 and binary 3 is 011. Their bitwise AND is 001, which is 1.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println(5 | 3); } }
explanation: Binary 101 OR 011 gives 111, which is decimal 7.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int a = 10; int b = 20; int max = (a > b) ? a : b; System.out.println(max); } }
explanation: The condition a > b is false, so the conditional operator selects b, which is 20.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int a = 5; int b = 2; double result = a / b; System.out.println(result); } }
explanation: Both operands are integers, so integer division produces 2 before assignment to double. The result becomes 2.0.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { char ch = 'A'; System.out.println((int)ch); } }
explanation: The Unicode value of the character A is 65.

question_text: Which assignment is valid in Java?
explanation: Java boolean variables accept only true or false values, not integers or strings.

question_text: What happens when this code is compiled? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int x; System.out.println(x); } }
explanation: Local variables must be initialized before they are read. Java does not automatically initialize local variables.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { static int x = 10; public static void main(String[] args) { int x = 20; System.out.println(x); } }
explanation: The local variable x shadows the static variable x within the main method.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int x = 5; int y = x++ + x++; System.out.println(y); } }
explanation: The first post-increment returns 5 and changes x to 6. The second returns 6 and changes x to 7. The sum is 11.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int x = 10; x *= 2 + 3; System.out.println(x); } }
explanation: Compound assignment evaluates the right-hand expression first: 2 + 3 = 5, then 10 multiplied by 5 gives 50.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println(10 + 2 * 3); } }
explanation: Multiplication has higher precedence than addition. Therefore 10 + 6 = 16.

question_text: Which primitive Java data type stores a single 16-bit Unicode character?
explanation: The char primitive type represents a single 16-bit UTF-16 code unit.

question_text: Which declaration is a valid main method signature for a standalone Java application?
explanation: The standard entry-point signature is public static void main(String[] args).

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println(args.length); } } Run using: java Test one two three
explanation: Three command-line arguments are supplied, so args.length is 3.

question_text: What is the output of javac Test.java?
explanation: The Java compiler converts source code into bytecode stored in a .class file.

question_text: Which file is normally produced after compiling Test.java successfully?
explanation: The Java compiler normally generates a class file containing bytecode.

question_text: Which command executes a compiled Java class named Test?
explanation: The java launcher starts the JVM and executes the specified class.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println(010); } }
explanation: An integer literal beginning with 0 is interpreted as octal. Octal 10 equals decimal 8.

question_text: Which suffix can be used to explicitly represent a long integer literal?
explanation: The L suffix identifies a long literal. Uppercase L is preferred for readability.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println('A' + 1); } }
explanation: The char A has numeric value 65. Adding 1 produces the integer 66.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println("Java\\nCode"); } }
option_b: Java and Code on separate lines
explanation: The escape sequence \\n moves the cursor to a new line.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int x = 7; String result = (x % 2 == 0) ? "Even" : "Odd"; System.out.println(result); } }
explanation: 7 % 2 is 1, so the condition is false and Odd is selected.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int x = 5; System.out.println(x > 10 && ++x > 5); System.out.println(x); } }
explanation: The first condition is false, so short-circuit AND skips ++x. Therefore x remains 5.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int x = 5; System.out.println(x < 10 || ++x > 5); System.out.println(x); } }
explanation: The first condition is true, so short-circuit OR skips ++x. Therefore x remains 5.

question_text: Which data type cannot be used directly as the selector expression in a traditional Java switch statement?
explanation: A traditional Java switch does not accept double as its selector type. int, char and String are supported.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { char ch = 'b'; switch(ch) { case 'a': System.out.print("A"); break; case 'b': System.out.print("B"); break; default: System.out.print("X"); } } }
explanation: The switch expression is the character b, so case 'b' executes.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int i = 3; while(i > 0) { System.out.print(i); i--; } } }
explanation: The loop prints 3, then 2, then 1 as i decreases.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int i = 0; while(i < 5) { i++; if(i == 3) break; System.out.print(i); } } }
explanation: The loop prints 1 and 2. When i becomes 3, break terminates the loop before printing it.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int i = 0; while(i < 4) { i++; if(i == 2) continue; System.out.print(i); } } }
explanation: The loop skips printing 2 because continue transfers control to the next iteration. It prints 1, 3 and 4.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int x = 4; System.out.println(x + 2 * 3 - 1); } }
explanation: Multiplication is evaluated first: 4 + 6 - 1 = 9.

question_text: What happens when this code is compiled? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int x = 10.5; System.out.println(x); } }
explanation: A double value cannot be assigned to an int without explicit casting because it may lose precision.

question_text: What is the default value of an instance variable of type boolean in Java?
explanation: An instance boolean variable receives the default value false.

question_text: What happens when this code is compiled? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { byte b = 10; b = b * 2; System.out.println(b); } }
explanation: Multiplication of byte values produces an int result. Assigning that int to byte requires an explicit cast.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { short s = 10; s += 5; System.out.println(s); } }
explanation: Compound assignment performs an implicit narrowing conversion, so s += 5 is valid and produces 15.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int a = 5; int b = ++a * 2; System.out.println(a + " " + b); } }
explanation: Pre-increment changes a to 6 before multiplication. Therefore b becomes 12 and the output is 6 12.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { char ch = 'A'; ch++; System.out.println(ch); } }
explanation: The increment operator increases the character's Unicode value by one, changing A to B.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println(5 / 2.0); } }
explanation: Since one operand is a double, floating-point division is performed and the result is 2.5.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int x = 5; System.out.println(x++ + 2 * 3); } }
explanation: Multiplication is evaluated first, producing 6. Post-increment returns the original x value 5, so the result is 11.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int a = 5; int b = 10; System.out.println(a < b && b > 5); } }
explanation: Both conditions are true, so the logical AND expression evaluates to true.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int a = 15; int b = 20; int result = (a > b) ? a : b; System.out.println(result); } }
explanation: The condition a > b is false, so the conditional operator selects b, which is 20.

question_text: What happens when this code is compiled? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int age = 20; if(age >= 18) System.out.println("Adult"); else System.out.println("Minor"); } }
explanation: The condition age >= 18 is true, so Adult is printed.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int n = 1; switch(n) { case 1: System.out.print("One"); break; case 2: System.out.print("Two"); break; default: System.out.print("Other"); } } }
explanation: The value 1 matches case 1. The break statement exits the switch.

question_text: What happens when this code is compiled? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int n = 2; switch(n) { case 1: System.out.println("A"); case 2: System.out.println("B"); default: System.out.println("C"); } } }
option_c: Prints A then B then C
explanation: Execution begins at case 2 and falls through to default because there is no break statement.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int sum = 0; for(int i = 1; i <= 4; i++) { sum += i; } System.out.println(sum); } }
explanation: The loop adds 1 + 2 + 3 + 4, producing 10.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int i = 1; int sum = 0; while(i <= 3) { sum += i; i++; } System.out.println(sum); } }
explanation: The loop adds 1, 2 and 3. The total is 6.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int i = 1; do { System.out.print(i); i++; } while(i <= 3); } }
explanation: The body executes for i values 1, 2 and 3. The output is 123.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { for(int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) { if(i % 2 == 0) continue; System.out.print(i); } } }
explanation: Continue skips even numbers. The loop prints 1, 3 and 5.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { int i = 1; while(true) { if(i == 4) break; System.out.print(i); i++; } } }
explanation: The loop prints 1, 2 and 3. When i reaches 4, break terminates the loop.

question_text: What happens when this code executes? class Test { public static void main(String[] args) { for(int i = 1; i <= 3; i-- ) { System.out.print(i); } } }
option_d: The loop does not terminate normally
explanation: The loop starts at 1 and decrements i. Since i remains less than or equal to 3, the condition stays true and the loop continues indefinitely.

question_text: Which declaration is invalid in Java?
explanation: A char literal must use single quotes. Double quotes create a String literal.

question_text: Which sequence correctly represents the basic Java compilation and execution process?
option_a: Source code to bytecode to JVM execution
option_b: Bytecode to source code to compiler
option_c: Source code to machine code directly to JVM
option_d: JVM to source code to compiler
explanation: The Java compiler converts source code into bytecode, which is then executed by the JVM.

question_text: What happens if a standalone Java application does not contain a valid main method?
option_b: The JVM cannot find the application entry point
option_d: The program executes from the first variable declaration
explanation: A standalone Java application needs a valid entry-point main method for normal launching.

question_text: Which statement correctly declares an integer array of size 5 in Java?
explanation: Java uses int[] arr = new int[5] to declare and create an integer array.

question_text: What is the index of the first element in a Java array?
explanation: Java arrays use zero-based indexing, so the first element is at index 0.

question_text: Which property is used to find the number of elements in an array?
explanation: The length property gives the number of elements in an array.

question_text: What is the default value of an element in a newly created int array?
explanation: Integer array elements are initialized to 0 by default.

question_text: What is the output? int[] a = {10, 20, 30}; System.out.println(a[1]);
explanation: Array indexing starts at zero, so a[1] refers to 20.

question_text: What is the output? int[] a = {2, 4, 6}; int sum = 0; for(int x : a) sum += x; System.out.println(sum);
explanation: The enhanced for loop adds 2 + 4 + 6, producing 12.

question_text: Which loop is commonly used to traverse every element of an array?
explanation: A for loop can access each array element using its index.

question_text: What happens when a program accesses an array index outside its valid range?
explanation: Accessing an invalid array index causes ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException at runtime.

question_text: What is the output? int[] a = {5, 10, 15}; a[1] = 25; System.out.println(a[1]);
explanation: The assignment changes the element at index 1 to 25.

question_text: How do you declare a two-dimensional integer array in Java?
explanation: The declaration int[][] represents a two-dimensional array.

question_text: What is the output? int[][] a = {{1,2},{3,4}}; System.out.println(a[1][0]);
explanation: Row 1 and column 0 contain the value 3.

question_text: What is a jagged array in Java?
option_a: An array with equal row sizes
option_b: An array of arrays with different row lengths
explanation: A jagged array is a multidimensional array whose rows can have different lengths.

question_text: Which package contains the String class?
explanation: String belongs to java.lang, which is imported automatically.

question_text: What does it mean that String objects are immutable?
option_b: Their contents cannot be changed after creation
explanation: String methods that appear to modify text return a new String instead.

question_text: What is the output? String s = "Java"; System.out.println(s.length());
explanation: The String Java contains four characters.

question_text: Which method returns the character at a specified index in a String?
explanation: charAt(index) returns the character at the given zero-based index.

question_text: Which method compares the contents of two String objects?
explanation: equals() compares String contents, whereas == compares object references.

question_text: What is the output? String s = "Java"; System.out.println(s.toUpperCase());
explanation: toUpperCase() returns a new String containing uppercase characters.

question_text: Which String method returns the index of the first occurrence of a specified character or substring?
explanation: indexOf() returns the first matching position, or -1 if not found.

question_text: What is the output? String a = "Hello"; String b = "Java"; System.out.println(a + " " + b);
explanation: The + operator joins the two strings with a space between them.

question_text: Which is a valid alternative syntax for declaring an integer array?
explanation: Java permits the array brackets after the variable name.

question_text: What is the output? int[] a = new int[3]; System.out.println(a[2]);
explanation: Every element of a newly created int array is initialized to zero.

question_text: What is the output? int[] a = {4, 8, 12, 16}; System.out.println(a.length);
explanation: The length property returns the number of array elements.

question_text: What happens when int[] a = {10,20}; and the program executes System.out.println(a[2]);?
explanation: Valid indices are 0 and 1. Index 2 is outside the array.

question_text: What is printed? int[] a = {2,4,6}; a[0] = a[2]; System.out.println(a[0]);
explanation: The value at index 2, which is 6, is assigned to index 0.

question_text: What is the output? int[] a = {1,2,3,4}; int s=0; for(int i=0;i<a.length;i++){s+=a[i];} System.out.println(s);
explanation: The loop adds all elements: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10.

question_text: What is the output? int[] a={2,3,4}; for(int x:a) System.out.print(x*2+" ");
explanation: The enhanced for loop visits each element and prints twice its value.

question_text: Which condition correctly checks whether arr[i] equals the key?
explanation: The == operator compares primitive integer values.

question_text: What is the output? int[] a={7,3,9,2}; int max=a[0]; for(int x:a){if(x>max) max=x;} System.out.println(max);
explanation: The loop updates max whenever it finds a larger element. The maximum is 9.

question_text: What is the output? int[] a={1,2,3}; int t=a[0]; a[0]=a[2]; a[2]=t; System.out.println(a[0]+" "+a[1]+" "+a[2]);
explanation: The first and last elements are swapped, producing 3 2 1.

question_text: What is wrong with this loop? int[] a={1,2,3}; for(int i=0;i<=a.length;i++){System.out.println(a[i]);}
option_b: The condition should be i < a.length
explanation: The last valid index is a.length - 1. Using <= causes an invalid index.

question_text: Which statement creates a new array containing the same elements as source?
explanation: clone() creates a separate array with copied element values.

question_text: What is the output? int[][] a={{1,2,3},{4,5,6}}; System.out.println(a.length);
explanation: For a two-dimensional array, length gives the number of rows.

question_text: What is the output? int[][] a={{1,2},{3,4}}; System.out.println(a[0].length);
explanation: The first row contains two elements.

question_text: How many elements are present in int[][] a={{1,2},{3,4},{5,6}};?
explanation: There are three rows with two elements each, giving six elements.

question_text: What is the output? int[][] a=new int[2][]; a[0]=new int[2]; a[1]=new int[3]; System.out.println(a[1].length);
explanation: The second row was created with three elements.

question_text: What is the output? int[][] a={{1,2},{3,4}}; int sum=0; for(int i=0;i<2;i++){for(int j=0;j<2;j++){sum+=a[i][j];}} System.out.println(sum);
explanation: The nested loops add 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10.

question_text: What is the default value of a boolean array element?
explanation: Boolean array elements are initialized to false.

question_text: What is the output? int[] a={1,2}; int[] b=a; b[0]=9; System.out.println(a[0]);
explanation: Both variables refer to the same array object, so the change is visible through a.

question_text: Which class provides the sort() method for sorting primitive arrays?
explanation: java.util.Arrays provides static utility methods such as sort().

question_text: Which statement creates a String object using the new keyword?
explanation: The String constructor can create a String object using new.

question_text: What is the output? String s="Java"; s.concat(" Programming"); System.out.println(s);
explanation: concat() returns a new String. Since the result is not assigned, s remains unchanged.

question_text: What is the output? String s="Hello"; s=s.concat(" World"); System.out.println(s);
explanation: The returned String is assigned back to s.

question_text: What is the output? String a="Java"; String b="Java"; System.out.println(a.equals(b));
explanation: equals() compares the character contents of the strings.

question_text: What does the expression a.compareTo(b) return when a and b contain equal strings?
explanation: compareTo() returns zero when the strings are lexicographically equal.

question_text: What is the output? String s="Programming"; System.out.println(s.indexOf('g'));
explanation: The first occurrence of g is at index 3.

question_text: What is the output? String s="Computer"; System.out.println(s.substring(0,4));
explanation: substring(0,4) includes indices 0 through 3, excluding index 4.

question_text: What is the output? String s=" Java "; System.out.println(s.trim().length());
explanation: trim() removes leading and trailing spaces, leaving Java with length 4.

question_text: Which method checks whether a String begins with a specified prefix?
explanation: startsWith() checks the beginning of a string.

question_text: What is the output? String s="Java"; System.out.println(s.contains("av"));
explanation: The substring av is present in Java.

question_text: Which method converts a String to lowercase?
explanation: toLowerCase() returns a lowercase version of the String.

question_text: Which method checks whether a String has zero characters?
explanation: isEmpty() returns true when the String length is zero.

question_text: What is the output? String s="HELLO"; System.out.println(s.charAt(4));
explanation: Index 4 contains the character O.

question_text: What is the output? String s="banana"; System.out.println(s.replace('a','o'));
explanation: replace() replaces every occurrence of a with o.

question_text: Which method splits a String into an array using a delimiter or regular expression?
explanation: split() divides a String into an array of substrings.

question_text: What is the output? String s="Java"; System.out.println(s.substring(2));
explanation: substring(2) returns the characters from index 2 to the end: va.

question_text: What is the String pool?
option_b: A special storage area for string literals
explanation: The String pool allows identical string literals to share stored objects.

question_text: What is the output? String a=new String("Java"); String b=new String("Java"); System.out.println(a==b);
explanation: new creates separate objects, so == compares different references.

question_text: What is the output? String a="Java"; String b="Java"; System.out.println(a==b);
explanation: Identical string literals are reused from the String pool.

question_text: Which statement about StringBuffer is correct?
explanation: StringBuffer is mutable, so its contents can be changed.

question_text: Which method adds text at the end of a StringBuffer?
explanation: append() adds the supplied value at the end of a StringBuffer.

question_text: What is the output? StringBuffer sb=new StringBuffer("Java"); sb.append(" SE"); System.out.println(sb);
explanation: append() modifies the existing StringBuffer by adding SE.

question_text: Which method inserts text at a specified position in a StringBuffer?
explanation: insert(index, value) inserts text at the specified position.

question_text: What is the output? StringBuffer sb=new StringBuffer("Java"); sb.reverse(); System.out.println(sb);
explanation: reverse() reverses the character sequence to avaJ.

question_text: Which method removes characters from a StringBuffer between two indexes?
explanation: delete(start,end) removes characters from start up to but excluding end.

question_text: Which method returns the current capacity of a StringBuffer?
explanation: capacity() returns the current allocated character capacity.

question_text: What is the output? StringBuffer sb=new StringBuffer("Hello"); System.out.println(sb.length());
explanation: The buffer contains five characters.

question_text: What is the output? StringBuffer sb=new StringBuffer("Code"); sb.setCharAt(0,'N'); System.out.println(sb);
explanation: setCharAt() replaces the character at index 0, producing Node.

question_text: Which statement is true about StringBuffer and String?
option_b: StringBuffer is mutable and String is immutable
option_c: String is mutable and StringBuffer is immutable
explanation: StringBuffer can be modified, whereas String objects cannot be changed.

question_text: Which keyword is used to define a class in Java?
explanation: The class keyword defines a class.

question_text: Which keyword is commonly used to create an object?
explanation: The new operator creates an object and invokes its constructor.

question_text: What is the purpose of the dot operator in Java?
option_b: To access members of an object
explanation: The dot operator accesses fields and methods through an object reference.

question_text: Where are instance variables declared?
option_b: Inside a class but outside methods
explanation: Instance variables are declared in the class body and belong to objects.

question_text: Where is a local variable declared?
explanation: A local variable is declared within a method, constructor, or block.

question_text: What is the output? class Test { int x=10; } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){ Test t=new Test(); System.out.println(t.x); }}
explanation: The object t accesses the instance variable x, whose value is 10.

question_text: Which part of a method declaration specifies the value returned by the method?
explanation: The return type specifies the type of value a method returns.

question_text: What is the output? class A { int add(int a,int b){return a+b;} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){ A obj=new A(); System.out.println(obj.add(3,4)); }}
explanation: The method returns 3 + 4, which is 7.

question_text: How is an instance method normally called from another class using an object?
explanation: An instance method is called using an object reference and the dot operator.

question_text: What is a constructor in Java?
option_a: A method with any return type
option_b: A special member used to initialize objects
explanation: A constructor initializes an object when it is created.

question_text: Which statement about a constructor is correct?
option_a: It must have the same name as its class
explanation: A constructor has the same name as its class and has no return type.

question_text: What happens if no constructor is declared in a class?
explanation: The compiler supplies a default no-argument constructor when no constructor is declared.

question_text: Which constructor accepts arguments?
explanation: A parameterized constructor accepts values to initialize an object.

question_text: What is the output? class A { A(){System.out.println("Created");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){ new A(); }}
explanation: Creating the object invokes its no-argument constructor.

question_text: What is constructor overloading?
option_a: Defining constructors with different parameter lists
explanation: Constructor overloading provides multiple constructors with different parameter lists.

question_text: Which feature allows a class to have both A() and A(int x)?
explanation: The constructors have different parameter lists, so they are overloaded.

question_text: What does this refer to in an instance method?
explanation: this refers to the current object.

question_text: What is the output? class A { int x; A(int x){this.x=x;} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){ A a=new A(15); System.out.println(a.x); }}
explanation: this.x refers to the instance variable, while x refers to the constructor parameter.

question_text: Where must a call to this() appear inside a constructor?
explanation: A constructor call using this() must be the first statement.

question_text: What is method overloading?
option_a: Same method name with different parameter lists
option_b: Same method name only in subclasses
explanation: Overloaded methods share a name but differ in parameter lists.

question_text: Can two methods be overloaded by changing only their return types?
explanation: Return type alone cannot distinguish overloaded methods.

question_text: What is the output? class A { int add(int a,int b){return a+b;} double add(double a,double b){return a+b;} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){ A a=new A(); System.out.println(a.add(2,3)); }}
explanation: The integer version is selected and returns 5.

question_text: Which is a valid overloaded method pair?
option_a: void show(int x) and void show(String x)
option_b: int add(int x) and double add(int x)
explanation: Different parameter types allow valid method overloading.

question_text: Can an object reference be passed as a method argument in Java?
explanation: Java methods can accept object references as parameters.

question_text: What is the output? class A { int x; } public class Main { static void change(A a){a.x=20;} public static void main(String[] args){A obj=new A(); obj.x=5; change(obj); System.out.println(obj.x);}}
explanation: The method receives a copy of the reference to the same object and modifies its field.

question_text: What is passed to a method when an object is supplied as an argument?
explanation: Java passes the reference value by value; the method can access the same object.

question_text: What is the default value of an instance variable of type int?
explanation: Instance variables of type int receive the default value zero.

question_text: What happens if a local variable is used before initialization?
explanation: Local variables must be initialized before they are used.

question_text: What is wrong with this code? class Student { void Student(){System.out.println("Hello");} }
option_b: It is a method and not a constructor
explanation: A constructor has no return type. void makes Student() an ordinary method.

question_text: What is the output? class A { void show(int x){System.out.print("I");} void show(double x){System.out.print("D");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){new A().show(5);}}
explanation: The integer argument selects show(int), so I is printed.

question_text: What is the output? class A { int x=5; } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){ A[] arr=new A[2]; System.out.println(arr[0]); }}
explanation: An array of object references initially contains null references.

question_text: Which keyword is used to refer to the current object's instance variable when a parameter has the same name?
explanation: this distinguishes the instance variable from a local parameter with the same name.

question_text: Can a constructor be overloaded with different parameter types?
explanation: Constructors can have different parameter lists, including different parameter types.

question_text: What is the output? String[] names={"Ram","Sam"}; System.out.println(names[1]);
explanation: Index 1 refers to the second element, Sam.

question_text: What is inheritance in Java?
option_b: Acquiring properties and methods of another class
explanation: Inheritance allows a class to acquire accessible members of another class.

question_text: Which keyword is used to inherit a class in Java?
explanation: The extends keyword is used for class inheritance.

question_text: Which class is known as the parent class?
explanation: The class whose members are inherited is called the superclass.

question_text: Which class inherits properties from another class?
explanation: A subclass inherits accessible members from its superclass.

question_text: Which type of inheritance is directly supported between Java classes?
explanation: Java supports multilevel inheritance through class extension.

question_text: Does Java support multiple inheritance through classes?
explanation: A Java class cannot extend more than one class.

question_text: Which feature allows a subclass to reuse superclass methods?
explanation: Inheritance promotes code reuse by allowing subclasses to use inherited methods.

question_text: What is the output? class A { void show(){System.out.print("A");} } class B extends A {} public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){new B().show();}}
explanation: B inherits the show method from A and executes it.

question_text: What is the output? class A { int x=10; } class B extends A {} public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){B obj=new B(); System.out.println(obj.x);}}
explanation: The subclass object can access the inherited public or package-accessible field.

question_text: Which members are not directly inherited by a subclass?
explanation: Constructors are not inherited by subclasses.

question_text: Which keyword refers to the immediate superclass object context?
explanation: super is used to access superclass members and constructors.

question_text: What is the output? class A { A(){System.out.print("A");} } class B extends A { B(){System.out.print("B");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){new B();}}
explanation: The superclass constructor executes before the subclass constructor.

question_text: What happens when a subclass constructor does not explicitly call super()?
option_b: Compiler inserts a super() call when applicable
explanation: The compiler inserts an implicit no-argument super() call when applicable.

question_text: Which statement about Java inheritance is correct?
option_a: A class can extend many classes
option_b: A class can extend one class
explanation: Java classes have only one direct superclass.

question_text: What is multilevel inheritance?
option_b: A class extends a class that already extends another class
explanation: Multilevel inheritance forms a chain of superclass and subclass relationships.

question_text: What is the output? class A { void show(){System.out.print("Hello");} } class B extends A {} class C extends B {} public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){new C().show();}}
explanation: C inherits show through B from A.

question_text: Which access modifier allows access from subclasses even when they are in different packages?
explanation: protected members are accessible in subclasses subject to Java access rules.

question_text: Can a private superclass field be directly accessed by its subclass?
explanation: Private members are not directly accessible in a subclass.

question_text: What is the purpose of the super keyword?
explanation: super provides access to superclass constructors and members.

question_text: Which statement about constructors in inheritance is correct?
option_b: Superclass constructor runs before subclass constructor
explanation: Superclass initialization occurs before subclass initialization.

question_text: What is the output? class A { int x=5; } class B extends A { int x=10; void show(){System.out.println(super.x);}} public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){new B().show();}}
explanation: super.x accesses the superclass field, whose value is 5.

question_text: What is method overriding?
option_a: Defining same method in unrelated classes
option_b: Redefining an inherited method in a subclass
explanation: Method overriding provides a subclass-specific implementation of an inherited method.

question_text: Which condition is required for method overriding?
option_a: Same method name and compatible parameters
explanation: An overriding method uses the same signature with a compatible return type.

question_text: What is the output? class A { void show(){System.out.print("A");} } class B extends A { void show(){System.out.print("B");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){new B().show();}}
explanation: The subclass version overrides the superclass method.

question_text: Can a static method be overridden in the same way as an instance method?
explanation: Static methods are hidden rather than overridden.

question_text: Which annotation is commonly used to indicate an overriding method?
explanation: The @Override annotation helps the compiler verify overriding.

question_text: Can an overriding method reduce the visibility of the inherited method?
explanation: An overriding method cannot have more restrictive access than the overridden method.

question_text: Can an overriding method use a covariant return type?
explanation: A covariant return type may be a subtype of the original method's return type.

question_text: What happens if a subclass method has the same name but different parameters?
explanation: Different parameter lists create an overloaded method rather than overriding.

question_text: What is dynamic method dispatch?
option_b: Runtime selection of an overridden method
explanation: The JVM selects the overridden instance method based on the actual object type at runtime.

question_text: What is the output? class A { void show(){System.out.print("A");} } class B extends A { void show(){System.out.print("B");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){A obj=new B(); obj.show();}}
explanation: The reference is A but the actual object is B, so B's overridden method executes.

question_text: In A obj = new B(), what determines the overridden instance method executed?
explanation: Dynamic dispatch uses the actual runtime object type.

question_text: Can dynamic method dispatch apply to overridden static methods?
explanation: Static methods are resolved using the reference or class type, not runtime dispatch.

question_text: What is the output? class A { void show(){System.out.print("A");} } class B extends A { void show(){System.out.print("B");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){A obj=new B(); ((A)obj).show();}}
explanation: Casting the reference to A does not change the actual object, which remains B.

question_text: What does super.show() call when show() is overridden in a subclass?
explanation: super.show() explicitly invokes the superclass implementation.

question_text: What is the output? class A { void show(){System.out.print("A");} } class B extends A { void show(){super.show(); System.out.print("B");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){new B().show();}}
explanation: The superclass method prints A first, followed by B.

question_text: What does final mean when applied to a class?
explanation: A final class cannot be subclassed.

question_text: What happens when a method is declared final?
explanation: A final method cannot be overridden by subclasses.

question_text: What is the output? final int x=10; x=20; System.out.println(x);
explanation: A final variable cannot be reassigned after initialization.

question_text: Can a final object reference point to a different object after initialization?
explanation: A final reference cannot be reassigned, although the referenced object's state may change.

question_text: Which keyword prevents a method from being overridden?
explanation: The final modifier prevents subclasses from overriding the method.

question_text: What is a static variable?
option_a: A variable created separately for every method
option_b: A class-level variable shared by instances
option_c: A variable that cannot be initialized
explanation: A static field belongs to the class and is shared by its instances.

question_text: How is a static variable commonly accessed?
explanation: A static variable can be accessed using the class name and dot operator.

question_text: What is the output? class A { static int count=0; A(){count++;} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){new A(); new A(); System.out.println(A.count);}}
explanation: Both objects increment the same static variable, resulting in 2.

question_text: Which statement about a static method is correct?
option_a: It requires an object to be called
explanation: A static method belongs to the class rather than an individual object.

question_text: Can a static method directly access a non-static instance variable?
explanation: A static method has no current object reference and cannot directly access instance members.

question_text: What is the output? class A { static void show(){System.out.print("Java");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){A.show();}}
explanation: The static method is called directly using the class name.

question_text: When is a static initialization block generally executed?
option_a: Every time an object is created
explanation: A static block runs during class initialization.

question_text: What is the output? class A { static {System.out.print("Static ");} A(){System.out.print("Object");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){new A();}}
explanation: The static block runs during class initialization before the constructor.

question_text: Which keyword declares a nested class that does not require an enclosing object instance?
explanation: A static nested class does not need an instance of the outer class.

question_text: Can a static method be overloaded?
explanation: Static methods can have multiple versions with different parameter lists.

question_text: Which keyword is used to declare an abstract class?
explanation: The abstract keyword declares an abstract class.

question_text: Can an abstract class be instantiated directly?
explanation: An abstract class cannot be instantiated directly.

question_text: What is an abstract method?
option_b: A method with only local variables
explanation: An abstract method is declared without an implementation body.

question_text: Which class must implement inherited abstract methods unless it is also abstract?
explanation: A concrete subclass must provide implementations for inherited abstract methods.

question_text: Can an abstract class contain constructors and concrete methods?
explanation: Abstract classes can contain constructors, fields, and concrete methods.

question_text: What happens if a concrete subclass does not implement an inherited abstract method?
option_b: It must be declared abstract or compilation fails
explanation: A concrete class must implement all inherited abstract methods.

question_text: Can an abstract method be declared final?
explanation: An abstract method must be overridden, while final prevents overriding.

question_text: Can an abstract method be private?
explanation: A private method cannot be overridden by a subclass, so it cannot serve as an abstract method.

question_text: What is the output? abstract class A { abstract void show(); } class B extends A { void show(){System.out.print("Done");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){A obj=new B(); obj.show();}}
explanation: B implements show(), and dynamic dispatch executes that implementation.

question_text: Which statement best describes an abstract class?
option_a: It must contain only abstract methods
option_b: It can contain both abstract and concrete methods
explanation: An abstract class may provide partial implementation and shared state.

question_text: Which keyword is used to declare an interface?
explanation: The interface keyword declares an interface.

question_text: Which keyword is used by a class to implement an interface?
explanation: A class uses implements to provide an interface implementation.

question_text: Can a Java class implement multiple interfaces?
explanation: A class can implement multiple interfaces.

question_text: What is the default visibility of an interface field?
explanation: Interface fields are implicitly public, static, and final.

question_text: Which type of method is traditionally abstract by default in an interface?
explanation: An ordinary interface method without a body is implicitly public and abstract.

question_text: Can an interface extend another interface?
explanation: An interface can extend one or more interfaces.

question_text: Can an interface extend multiple interfaces?
explanation: An interface may extend multiple interfaces.

question_text: Can a class extend an interface directly?
explanation: A class implements an interface; it does not extend it.

question_text: What is the output? interface A { void show(); } class B implements A { public void show(){System.out.print("Hello");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){A obj=new B(); obj.show();}}
explanation: B implements the interface method, and the interface reference calls it.

question_text: Why must an implemented interface method generally be declared public?
explanation: The implementation cannot reduce the public visibility required by the interface.

question_text: Can an interface contain default methods with implementations?
explanation: Default methods allow interfaces to provide method implementations.

question_text: Which keyword identifies an interface default method?
explanation: The default keyword is used to declare a default interface method.

question_text: Can an interface contain static methods?
explanation: Interfaces can declare static methods with implementations.

question_text: How is a static interface method normally called?
explanation: Static interface methods are called using the interface name.

question_text: Can an interface have a constructor?
explanation: Interfaces cannot be instantiated and do not have constructors.

question_text: What happens if a class implements an interface but does not implement all its abstract methods?
option_b: It must be abstract or compilation fails
explanation: A non-abstract class must implement all inherited abstract methods.

question_text: What is the output? interface A { int X=10; } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){System.out.println(A.X);}}
explanation: Interface fields are public static final and can be accessed using the interface name.

question_text: Can an interface extend two interfaces named A and B?
explanation: An interface can extend multiple interfaces using a comma-separated list.

question_text: What is a nested interface?
option_a: An interface declared inside another type
explanation: A nested interface is declared within another class or interface.

question_text: Which relationship is represented when a class implements an interface?
explanation: Implementing an interface means the class agrees to provide the required behavior.

question_text: What does polymorphism mean in Java?
explanation: Polymorphism allows the same interface or method call to represent different behaviors.

question_text: Which feature is an example of compile-time polymorphism?
explanation: Method overloading is resolved at compile time.

question_text: Which feature is an example of runtime polymorphism?
explanation: Overridden instance methods are selected at runtime.

question_text: What is the output? class A { void show(){System.out.print("A");} } class B extends A { void show(){System.out.print("B");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){A x=new B(); x.show();}}
explanation: Runtime polymorphism selects the B implementation.

question_text: What is an upcasting operation?
option_a: Subclass reference assigned to superclass reference
option_b: Superclass reference assigned to unrelated class
explanation: Upcasting treats a subclass object through a superclass reference.

question_text: Is upcasting generally performed automatically in Java?
explanation: A subclass object can be assigned to a compatible superclass reference automatically.

question_text: What is downcasting?
option_a: Converting superclass reference to subclass reference
explanation: Downcasting explicitly converts a superclass reference to a subclass reference.

question_text: Which operator can check whether an object is an instance of a particular type?
explanation: instanceof checks whether an object is compatible with a specified type.

question_text: What happens when an invalid downcast is attempted at runtime?
explanation: An incompatible runtime cast can cause ClassCastException.

question_text: What is the output? class A {} class B extends A {} public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){A obj=new B(); System.out.println(obj instanceof B);}}
explanation: The actual object is an instance of B.

question_text: Can a superclass reference access a subclass-only method without casting?
explanation: The compiler checks accessible members using the reference's declared type.

question_text: What determines which overloaded method is selected?
option_b: Compile-time argument types and method signatures
explanation: Overload resolution is performed at compile time using argument types.

question_text: What is the output? class A { void show(int x){System.out.print("Int");} void show(double x){System.out.print("Double");} } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){new A().show(5);}}
explanation: The int argument selects show(int).

question_text: Can constructors be overridden?
explanation: Constructors are not inherited, so they cannot be overridden.

question_text: Can private methods be overridden by subclasses?
explanation: Private methods are not inherited as accessible methods and cannot be overridden.

question_text: What is the output? class A { int x=10; } class B extends A { int x=20; } public class Main { public static void main(String[] args){A obj=new B(); System.out.println(obj.x);}}
explanation: Fields are hidden rather than dynamically dispatched; the reference type A determines the field accessed.

question_text: Can a final class implement an interface?
option_d: Only if it has no methods
explanation: final prevents subclassing but does not prevent interface implementation.

question_text: Can an abstract class implement an interface without implementing every method?
explanation: An abstract class may leave interface methods unimplemented for subclasses.

question_text: What happens if two implemented interfaces provide conflicting default methods with the same signature?
option_b: The class must resolve the conflict
option_d: The program always uses the first interface
explanation: The implementing class must override the conflicting default method.

question_text: How can a class explicitly call a particular interface's default method when resolving a conflict?
explanation: InterfaceName.super.method() invokes that interface's default implementation.

question_text: Which statement best describes the is-a relationship?
option_a: A subclass is a type of its superclass
explanation: Inheritance models an is-a relationship between a subclass and superclass.
